topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and the origins of susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations accumulate and confer clonal advantages within the biological conditions that permit cancer to develop.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and their interpretation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the contribution of environmental exposures to cancer risk and how evidence for that contribution should be interpreted.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a detailed example.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce DNA damage that can become cancer-promoting mutations.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutational initiation from the promotional conditions that allow initiated cells to proliferate into tumours.

topics.label: Context-dependent susceptibility and synthesis of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics conclude the account of carcinogenic mechanisms by explaining how their effects depend on the biological context of exposure.

topics.label: Methods for investigating carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence and methods used to establish whether an exposure can cause cancer, including their limitations.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and placing cancer risks within everyday risk–benefit decisions.
